description: The manifest's own contractDigest ('ccf13ebd7393b923409f2b1395388b649303d5aa85e80039531b265e849b2906') does not match the actual sha256 of contracts/sprint-2.md as currently found on disk (independently computed this round: '03c072c4dbbe9462f1c7bbf3bf8b6b21c29c6e11340e094b2fcbc3e085436adb'). The contract file itself contains a 'Phase 2c refactor note (this revision)' section at its own tail (lines 162-204) describing the activeStatusFields extraction and the two independently-re-verified GREEN-phase implementation notes -- content that was evidently appended AFTER whatever earlier version of the file the manifest's digest was computed against (most likely the Phase 1c-approved pre-refactor version). This is most likely a process/tooling gap (the digest was never recomputed when the contract was revised to add the Phase 2c note) rather than a sign of unauthorized tampering, but it does mean the digest recorded in the manifest cannot currently be used as a tamper-evidence check against the artifact actually reviewed this round.

crossCheck.note: Computed via `shasum -a 256 contracts/sprint-2.md` against the file as currently committed on ~/anicca-project's working tree this session; does not match the manifest's recorded digest.

resolutionRecommendation: Recompute and update the contractDigest recorded wherever this sprint's contract review round is tracked (manifest and/or state.json) to match the current, Phase-2c-revised contracts/sprint-2.md content, so future rounds' tamper-evidence checks are meaningful. Does not block this round's verdict on its own -- the actual content reviewed this round is the current, complete file (including the Phase 2c note), which is the correct artifact to review regardless of the stale digest.
